numbered.requirement: The character data in a UTF-8 Encoded String MUST be well-formed UTF-8 as defined by the Unicode specification [Unicode] and restated in RFC 3629 [RFC3629]. In particular, the character data MUST NOT include encodings of code points between U+D800 and U+DFFF
numbered.observation: Strings validate UTF-8/NUL and preserve exact input bytes, including BOM and normalization.

numbered.requirement: A UTF-8 Encoded String MUST NOT include an encoding of the null character U+0000
numbered.observation: Strings validate UTF-8/NUL and preserve exact input bytes, including BOM and normalization.

numbered.requirement: A UTF-8 encoded sequence 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF is always interpreted as U+FEFF ("ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE") wherever it appears in a string and MUST NOT be skipped over or stripped off by a packet receiver
numbered.observation: Strings validate UTF-8/NUL and preserve exact input bytes, including BOM and normalization.

numbered.requirement: The Variable Byte Integer is encoded using an encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127. Larger values are handled as follows. The least significant seven bits of each byte encode the data, and the most significant bit is used to indicate whether there are bytes following in the representation. Thus, each byte encodes 128 values and a "continuation bit". The maximum number of bytes in the Variable Byte Integer field is four. The encoded value MUST use the minimum number of bytes necessary to represent the value
numbered.observation: Minimal VBI width and four-octet maximum are checked before body allocation.

numbered.requirement: Both strings MUST comply with the requirements for UTF-8 Encoded Strings
numbered.observation: Both ordered User Property components use the same UTF-8 primitive.

numbered.requirement: The remaining bits [3-0] of byte 1 in the Fixed Header contain flags specific to each MQTT Control Packet type as shown below. Where a flag bit is marked as “Reserved”, it is reserved for future use and MUST be set to the value listed
numbered.observation: Fixed flags are table-validated; operational owners close decoder failures.

numbered.requirement: A PUBLISH packet MUST NOT contain a Packet Identifier if its QoS value is set to 0
numbered.observation: QoS0 PUBLISH encodes no identifier; an explicit local identifier rejects.

numbered.requirement: Each time a Client sends a new SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE,or PUBLISH (where QoS > 0) MQTT Control Packet it MUST assign it a non-zero Packet Identifier that is currently unused
numbered.observation: Client allocator reserves IDs across SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE and QoS1/2 PUBLISH, including surviving protocol-only operations.

numbered.requirement: Each time a Server sends a new PUBLISH (with QoS > 0) MQTT Control Packet it MUST assign it a non zero Packet Identifier that is currently unused
numbered.observation: Session-local outgoing IDs are independently allocated and remain reserved until completion.

numbered.requirement: A PUBACK, PUBREC , PUBREL, or PUBCOMP packet MUST contain the same Packet Identifier as the PUBLISH packet that was originally sent
numbered.observation: ACK/REL/COMP constructors reuse the incoming or saved publication identifier.

numbered.requirement: A SUBACK and UNSUBACK MUST contain the Packet Identifier that was used in the corresponding SUBSCRIBE and UNSUBSCRIBE packet respectively
numbered.observation: Broker ACKs use the request ID; client correlates that ID to the pending request.

numbered.requirement: The Property Length is encoded as a Variable Byte Integer. The Property Length does not include the bytes used to encode itself, but includes the length of the Properties. If there are no properties, this MUST be indicated by including a Property Length of zero
numbered.observation: Property Length is a canonical VBI, including explicit zero where the packet tail requires it; compact ACK omission follows its schema.

numbered.requirement: After a Network Connection is established by a Client to a Server, the first packet sent from the Client to the Server MUST be a CONNECT packet
numbered.observation: Client transport-up emits CONNECT; broker refuses non-CONNECT before authentication.

numbered.requirement: A Client can only send the CONNECT packet once over a Network Connection. The Server MUST process a second CONNECT packet sent from a Client as a Protocol Error and close the Network Connection
numbered.observation: Only the initial :connect phase accepts CONNECT; another CONNECT closes.

numbered.requirement: A Server which support multiple protocols uses the Protocol Name to determine whether the data is MQTT. The protocol name MUST be the UTF-8 String "MQTT". If the Server does not want to accept the CONNECT, and wishes to reveal that it is an MQTT Server it MAY send a CONNACK packet with Reason Code of 0x84 (Unsupported Protocol Version), and then it MUST close the Network Connection
numbered.observation: Codec validates protocol name/level/reserved flag; runtime accepts MQTT5 only and closes unsupported input.

numbered.requirement: A Server which supports multiple versions of the MQTT protocol uses the Protocol Version to determine which version of MQTT the Client is using. If the Protocol Version is not 5 and the Server does not want to accept the CONNECT packet, the Server MAY send a CONNACK packet with Reason Code 0x84 (Unsupported Protocol Version) and then MUST close the Network Connection
numbered.observation: Codec validates protocol name/level/reserved flag; runtime accepts MQTT5 only and closes unsupported input.

numbered.requirement: The Server MUST validate that the reserved flag in the CONNECT packet is set to 0
numbered.observation: Codec validates protocol name/level/reserved flag; runtime accepts MQTT5 only and closes unsupported input.

numbered.requirement: If a CONNECT packet is received with Clean Start is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any existing Session and start a new Session
numbered.observation: Clean Start creates new state; old protocol responsibility is not reported as successful.

numbered.requirement: If a CONNECT packet is received with Clean Start set to 0 and there is a Session associated with the Client Identifier, the Server MUST resume communications with the Client based on state from the existing Session
numbered.observation: Existing unexpired state is resumed for Clean Start0; absent/expired state is freshly created.

numbered.requirement: If a CONNECT packet is received with Clean Start set to 0 and there is no Session associated with the Client Identifier, the Server MUST create a new Session
numbered.observation: Existing unexpired state is resumed for Clean Start0; absent/expired state is freshly created.

numbered.requirement: If the Will Flag is set to 1 this indicates that a Will Message MUST be stored on the Server and associated with the Session
numbered.observation: Will fields are serialized together; broker registers, schedules, publishes and removes the session-associated Will.

numbered.requirement: The Will Message consists of the Will Properties, Will Topic, and Will Payload fields in the CONNECT Payload. The Will Message MUST be published after the Network Connection is subsequently closed and either the Will Delay Interval has elapsed or the Session ends, unless the Will Message has been deleted by the Server on receipt of a DISCONNECT packet with Reason Code 0x00 (Normal disconnection) or a new Network Connection for the ClientID is opened before the Will Delay Interval has elapsed
numbered.observation: Will fields are serialized together; broker registers, schedules, publishes and removes the session-associated Will.

numbered.requirement: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will Properties, Will Topic, and Will Payload fields MUST be present in the Payload
numbered.observation: Will fields are serialized together; broker registers, schedules, publishes and removes the session-associated Will.

numbered.requirement: The Will Message MUST be removed from the stored Session State in the Server once it has been published or the Server has received a DISCONNECT packet with a Reason Code of 0x00 (Normal disconnection) from the Client
numbered.observation: Will fields are serialized together; broker registers, schedules, publishes and removes the session-associated Will.

numbered.requirement: If the Will Flag is set to 0, then the Will QoS MUST be set to 0 (0x00)
numbered.observation: CONNECT encoder derives Will bits from presence/QoS/retain; decoder rejects inconsistent flags and QoS3.

numbered.requirement: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the value of Will QoS can be 0 (0x00), 1 (0x01), or 2 (0x02)
numbered.observation: CONNECT encoder derives Will bits from presence/QoS/retain; decoder rejects inconsistent flags and QoS3.

numbered.requirement: If the Will Flag is set to 0, then Will Retain MUST be set to 0
numbered.observation: CONNECT encoder derives Will bits from presence/QoS/retain; decoder rejects inconsistent flags and QoS3.

numbered.requirement: If the Will Flag is set to 1 and Will Retain is set to 0, the Server MUST publish the Will Message as a non-retained message
numbered.observation: Will retain flag is copied into the constructed publication and normal retained admission.

numbered.requirement: If the Will Flag is set to 1 and Will Retain is set to 1, the Server MUST publish the Will Message as a retained message
numbered.observation: Will retain flag is copied into the constructed publication and normal retained admission.

numbered.requirement: If the User Name Flag is set to 0, a User Name MUST NOT be present in the Payload
numbered.observation: Credential flag/presence derives from nil versus present value, including empty values; decoder consumes fields in order.

numbered.requirement: If the User Name Flag is set to 1, a User Name MUST be present in the Payload
numbered.observation: Credential flag/presence derives from nil versus present value, including empty values; decoder consumes fields in order.

numbered.requirement: If the Password Flag is set to 0, a Password MUST NOT be present in the Payload
numbered.observation: Credential flag/presence derives from nil versus present value, including empty values; decoder consumes fields in order.

numbered.requirement: If the Password Flag is set to 1, a Password MUST be present in the Payload
numbered.observation: Credential flag/presence derives from nil versus present value, including empty values; decoder consumes fields in order.

numbered.requirement: The Keep Alive is a Two Byte Integer which is a time interval measured in seconds. It is the maximum time interval that is permitted to elapse between the point at which the Client finishes transmitting one MQTT Control Packet and the point it starts sending the next. It is the responsibility of the Client to ensure that the interval between MQTT Control Packets being sent does not exceed the Keep Alive value. If Keep Alive is non-zero and in the absence of sending any other MQTT Control Packets, the Client MUST send a PINGREQ packet
numbered.observation: Client tick sends PINGREQ after the negotiated nonzero interval without completed outgoing traffic.

numbered.requirement: If the Server returns a Server Keep Alive on the CONNACK packet, the Client MUST use that value instead of the value it sent as the Keep Alive
numbered.observation: Negotiated Server Keep Alive replaces the CONNECT interval.

numbered.requirement: If the Keep Alive value is non-zero and the Server does not receive an MQTT Control Packet from the Client within one and a half times the Keep Alive time period, it MUST close the Network Connection to the Client as if the network had failed
numbered.observation: Broker uses complete-packet last_seen and closes at 1.5× nonzero Keep Alive.

numbered.requirement: The Client and Server MUST store the Session State after the Network Connection is closed if the Session Expiry Interval is greater than 0
numbered.observation: Nonzero expiry preserves session state after transport closure; local-durable profile separately persists it.

numbered.requirement: The Server MUST NOT send packets exceeding Maximum Packet Size to the Client
numbered.observation: Control writes respect peer bound; oversized onward Application Messages retire locally without closing a healthy recipient.

numbered.requirement: Where a Packet is too large to send, the Server MUST discard it without sending it and then behave as if it had completed sending that Application Message
numbered.observation: Control writes respect peer bound; oversized onward Application Messages retire locally without closing a healthy recipient.

numbered.requirement: This value indicates the highest value that the Client will accept as a Topic Alias sent by the Server. The Client uses this value to limit the number of Topic Aliases that it is willing to hold on this Connection. The Server MUST NOT send a Topic Alias in a PUBLISH packet to the Client greater than Topic Alias Maximum
numbered.observation: Broker never emits aliases; valid for any client maximum including absent/zero.
numbered.uncovered: No positive alias mapping is claimed or required with negotiated maximum0.

numbered.requirement: A value of 0 indicates that the Client does not accept any Topic Aliases on this connection. If Topic Alias Maximum is absent or zero, the Server MUST NOT send any Topic Aliases to the Client
numbered.observation: Broker never emits aliases; valid for any client maximum including absent/zero.
numbered.uncovered: No positive alias mapping is claimed or required with negotiated maximum0.

numbered.requirement: The Client uses this value to request the Server to return Response Information in the CONNACK. A value of 0 indicates that the Server MUST NOT return Response Information
numbered.observation: Broker omits Response Information regardless of Request Response Information; the prohibition at0 is satisfied by omission.

numbered.requirement: If the value of Request Problem Information is 0, the Server MAY return a Reason String or User Properties on a CONNACK or DISCONNECT packet, but MUST NOT send a Reason String or User Properties on any packet other than PUBLISH, CONNACK, or DISCONNECT
numbered.observation: Broker emits no diagnostic Reason String/User Property ACKs; client checks forbidden ACK properties when requested off.

numbered.requirement: If a Client sets an Authentication Method in the CONNECT, the Client MUST NOT send any packets other than AUTH or DISCONNECT packets until it has received a CONNACK packet
numbered.observation: Client rejects Authentication Method/Data before starting a transport.

numbered.requirement: The Payload of the CONNECT packet contains one or more length-prefixed fields, whose presence is determined by the flags in the Variable Header. These fields, if present, MUST appear in the order Client Identifier, Will Properties, Will Topic, Will Payload, User Name, Password
numbered.observation: CONNECT payload encode/decode order is client ID, Will fields, username, password.

numbered.requirement: The Client Identifier (ClientID) identifies the Client to the Server. Each Client connecting to the Server has a unique ClientID. The ClientID MUST be used by Clients and by Servers to identify state that they hold relating to this MQTT Session between the Client and the Server
numbered.observation: Client ID keys local/remote session responsibility; broker separates principal and connection identity.

numbered.requirement: The ClientID MUST be present and is the first field in the CONNECT packet Payload
numbered.observation: Client ID is the first required payload string and retains UTF-8 bytes.

numbered.requirement: The ClientID MUST be a UTF-8 Encoded String as defined in section 1.5.4
numbered.observation: Client ID is the first required payload string and retains UTF-8 bytes.

numbered.requirement: The Server MUST allow ClientID’s which are between 1 and 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes in length, and that contain only the characters "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
numbered.observation: No additional alphanumeric1..23 restriction is imposed; all valid such IDs pass codec and normal authentication policy.

numbered.requirement: A Server MAY allow a Client to supply a ClientID that has a length of zero bytes, however if it does so the Server MUST treat this as a special case and assign a unique ClientID to that Client
numbered.observation: Empty client IDs are assigned a noncolliding ID and returned in successful CONNACK.

numbered.requirement: It MUST then process the CONNECT packet as if the Client had provided that unique ClientID, and MUST return the Assigned Client Identifier in the CONNACK packet
numbered.observation: Empty client IDs are assigned a noncolliding ID and returned in successful CONNACK.

numbered.requirement: If the Server rejects the ClientID it MAY respond to the CONNECT packet with a CONNACK using Reason Code 0x85 (Client Identifier not valid) as described in section 4.13 Handling errors, and then it MUST close the Network Connection
numbered.observation: Any rejection path closes; this profile does not otherwise restrict valid Client ID syntax.

numbered.requirement: The Server delays publishing the Client’s Will Message until the Will Delay Interval has passed or the Session ends, whichever happens first. If a new Network Connection to this Session is made before the Will Delay Interval has passed, the Server MUST NOT send the Will Message
numbered.observation: Reconnect before due time cancels the delayed old Will; expiry can trigger it earlier.

numbered.requirement: The Server MUST maintain the order of User Properties when publishing the Will Message
numbered.observation: Will properties are copied in order while removing only Will Delay. Direct regression retains repeated identical/different User Property values and PFI1; g7-mqtt-will-user-properties.log53/0.
numbered.uncovered: Bounded pure transition regression; no independent Will-order test claimed.

numbered.requirement: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Will Topic is the next field in the Payload. The Will Topic MUST be a UTF-8 Encoded String as defined in section 1.5.4
numbered.observation: Will Topic and present User Name use the UTF-8 primitive; Will Topic also rejects empty/wildcard names.

numbered.requirement: If the User Name Flag is set to 1, the User Name is the next field in the Payload. The User Name MUST be a UTF-8 Encoded String as defined in section 1.5.4
numbered.observation: Will Topic and present User Name use the UTF-8 primitive; Will Topic also rejects empty/wildcard names.

numbered.requirement: 2. The Server MUST validate that the CONNECT packet matches the format described in section 3.1 and close the Network Connection if it does not match
numbered.observation: Malformed CONNECT is refused by decoder/owner without session creation.

numbered.requirement: The Server MAY check that the contents of the CONNECT packet meet any further restrictions and SHOULD perform authentication and authorization checks. If any of these checks fail, it MUST close the Network Connection
numbered.observation: Authentication/authorization refusal or infrastructure error closes, without attaching a successful session.

numbered.requirement: 1. If the ClientID represents a Client already connected to the Server, the Server sends a DISCONNECT packet to the existing Client with Reason Code of 0x8E (Session taken over) as described in section 4.13 and MUST close the Network Connection of the existing Client
numbered.observation: Authenticated same-principal takeover disconnects the former connection; mismatched principal cannot take it over.

numbered.requirement: 2. The Server MUST perform the processing of Clean Start that is described in section 3.1.2.4
numbered.observation: Attach applies Clean Start before constructing Session Present.

numbered.requirement: 3. The Server MUST acknowledge the CONNECT packet with a CONNACK packet containing a 0x00 (Success) Reason Code
numbered.observation: Successful attach constructs CONNACK0 before pumping session deliveries.

numbered.requirement: Clients are allowed to send further MQTT Control Packets immediately after sending a CONNECT packet; Clients need not wait for a CONNACK packet to arrive from the Server. If the Server rejects the CONNECT, it MUST NOT process any data sent by the Client after the CONNECT packet except AUTH packets
numbered.observation: Rejected CONNECT removes/closes connection; subsequent old input cannot be admitted.

numbered.requirement: The CONNACK packet is the packet sent by the Server in response to a CONNECT packet received from a Client. The Server MUST send a CONNACK with a 0x00 (Success) Reason Code before sending any Packet other than AUTH
numbered.observation: Successful attach queues one CONNACK before any delivery; another CONNECT cannot create another successful ACK.

numbered.requirement: The Server MUST NOT send more than one CONNACK in a Network Connection
numbered.observation: Successful attach queues one CONNACK before any delivery; another CONNECT cannot create another successful ACK.

numbered.requirement: Byte 1 is the "Connect Acknowledge Flags". Bits 7-1 are reserved and MUST be set to 0
numbered.observation: CONNACK codec masks/validates all reserved acknowledge flags.

numbered.requirement: If the Server accepts a connection with Clean Start set to 1, the Server MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet in addition to setting a 0x00 (Success) Reason Code in the CONNACK packet
numbered.observation: Session Present is exactly existing unexpired state AND not Clean Start.

numbered.requirement: If the Server accepts a connection with Clean Start set to 0 and the Server has Session State for the ClientID, it MUST set Session Present to 1 in the CONNACK packet, otherwise it MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet. In both cases it MUST set a 0x00 (Success) Reason Code in the CONNACK packet
numbered.observation: Session Present is exactly existing unexpired state AND not Clean Start.

numbered.requirement: If the Client does not have Session State and receives Session Present set to 1 it MUST close the Network Connection
numbered.observation: Session Present1 without a local session stops with local_session_missing, no connected event and no retry. Direct pure and real socket assertions; g7-mqtt-session-present.log pure38/client13 all0.
numbered.uncovered: Raw TCP fixture establishes this exact refusal boundary; it is not conforming external-peer interoperability evidence.

numbered.requirement: If the Client does have Session State and receives Session Present set to 0 it MUST discard its Session State if it continues with the Network Connection
numbered.observation: Successful CONNACK without Session Present resets old outgoing, incoming and subscription state.

numbered.requirement: If a Server sends a CONNACK packet containing a non-zero Reason Code it MUST set Session Present to 0
numbered.observation: Negative CONNACK cannot encode Session Present; broker rejects with false.

numbered.requirement: The values the Connect Reason Code are shown below. If a well formed CONNECT packet is received by the Server, but the Server is unable to complete the Connection the Server MAY send a CONNACK packet containing the appropriate Connect Reason code from this table. If a Server sends a CONNACK packet containing a Reason code of 128 or greater it MUST then close the Network Connection
